# Accuracy by exposures across age {#sec-exposure-age}

{{< include _caution.qmd >}}

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
i_am("notebooks/04-exposure-by-age.qmd")  # _quarto.yml would otherwise make notebooks/ the root
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(broom.mixed)

theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

novel_trials <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "novel_trials.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

AGE_BREAKS <- c(12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 60)
```

## The model

$$
\text{acc}_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \log(T_{ij} + 1) + \beta_2 \log(\text{age}_i / 24)
  + \beta_3 \log(T_{ij} + 1)\log(\text{age}_i / 24)
  + u_{\text{dataset}} + u_{\text{child}} + u_{\text{word}} + \epsilon_{ij}
$$

Here acc is long-window accuracy on test trial *j* for child *i*, and *T* is the number of teaching
exposures to the target word before that trial. Age is centered at 24 months on the log scale, so
$\beta_1$ is the exposure effect for a 2-year-old. The primary analysis uses **N–N test trials** only,
restricted to 12–36 months (ages up to 60 months are shown in the descriptives). Trials whose
teaching count is not yet coded (external teaching pending) are dropped and listed below.

```{r}
#| label: analysis-data
nn <- novel_trials |>
  filter(role == "test_nn", age >= 12, age <= 60) |>
  mutate(age_bin = cut(age, AGE_BREAKS, right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
         log_teaching = log(teaching + 1),
         log_age = log(age / 24))

nn |>
  filter(is.na(teaching)) |>
  count(dataset_name, name = "trials_with_uncoded_teaching")

nn <- nn |> filter(!is.na(teaching))
```

## Coverage

How many trials, children, and datasets support each cell of the exposures × age grid?

```{r}
#| label: coverage
nn |>
  summarise(n_trials = n(), n_children = n_distinct(subject_id),
            n_datasets = n_distinct(dataset_name),
            .by = c(age_bin, teaching)) |>
  arrange(age_bin, teaching)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Number of N–N test trials by teaching exposures and age, colored by dataset."
nn |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = teaching + 1, colour = dataset_name)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .3, height = .03, alpha = .3, size = .8) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, 33), labels = \(x) x - 1) +
  labs(x = "Age (months)", y = "Teaching exposures (log scale)", colour = "Dataset")
```

## Descriptive curves

Child-level means within each age bin × exposure cell, averaged across children.

```{r}
#| label: fig-curves
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy on N–N test trials by number of prior teaching exposures, by age bin. Points are means across children (±95% CI); point size is the number of children. The dashed line is chance."
by_child <- nn |>
  summarise(acc = mean(long_window_accuracy), .by = c(age_bin, teaching, subject_id))

curves <- by_child |>
  summarise(mean = mean(acc), n = n(),
            ci = 1.96 * sd(acc) / sqrt(n),
            .by = c(age_bin, teaching))

curves |>
  ggplot(aes(x = teaching + 1, y = mean, colour = age_bin)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean - ci, ymax = mean + ci),
                 position = position_dodge(width = .05), alpha = .5) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), position = position_dodge(width = .05)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = .05)) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, 33), labels = \(x) x - 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = .9) +
  labs(x = "Teaching exposures before test (log scale)",
       y = "Proportion target looking (200–4000 ms)",
       colour = "Age (months)", size = "Children")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-curves-dataset
#| fig-cap: "The same curves by dataset."
#| fig-height: 7
nn |>
  summarise(acc = mean(long_window_accuracy), .by = c(dataset_name, age_bin, teaching, subject_id)) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(acc), n = n(), .by = c(dataset_name, age_bin, teaching)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = teaching + 1, y = mean, colour = age_bin)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dataset_name) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, 33), labels = \(x) x - 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = .9) +
  labs(x = "Teaching exposures (log scale)", y = "Proportion target looking",
       colour = "Age (months)", size = "Children")
```

## Mixed-effects model

```{r}
#| label: model
nn_model <- nn |> filter(age <= 36)

m <- lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_teaching * log_age +
            (1 | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id) + (1 | target_label),
          data = nn_model)

tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-model
#| fig-cap: "Model predictions (fixed effects) for accuracy by teaching exposures at representative ages, each over the range of exposures observed within 3 months of that age."
# each age's curve spans the teaching range observed within 3 months of that age
pred_grid <- tibble(age = c(15, 21, 27, 33)) |>
  mutate(teaching = map(age, \(a) {
    obs <- nn_model$teaching[abs(nn_model$age - a) <= 3]
    seq(min(obs), max(obs), length.out = 50)
  })) |>
  unnest(teaching) |>
  mutate(log_age = log(age / 24), log_teaching = log(teaching + 1))

pred_grid$pred <- predict(m, newdata = pred_grid, re.form = NA)

pred_grid |>
  ggplot(aes(x = teaching + 1, y = pred, colour = factor(age))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, 33), labels = \(x) x - 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = .9) +
  labs(x = "Teaching exposures (log scale)", y = "Predicted proportion target looking",
       colour = "Age (months)")
```

## Sensitivity

Teaching varies mostly *between* datasets: most datasets have one or two teaching levels. Only
`reflook_socword`, `adams_marchman_2018`, `fernald_marchman_2012`, and `fernald_totlot` vary it within
the dataset. Two checks on the primary model:

* **observed**: teaching counted only from trials present in Peekbank, without the reconstructed
  missing trials (@sec-exposure)
* **within-dataset**: dataset as a fixed effect, so the teaching slope is estimated only from
  within-dataset variation

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity
m_observed <- lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_teaching_observed * log_age +
                     (1 | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id) + (1 | target_label),
                   data = nn_model |> mutate(log_teaching_observed = log(teaching_observed + 1)))

m_within <- lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_teaching * log_age + dataset_name +
                   (1 | subject_id) + (1 | target_label),
                 data = nn_model)

bind_rows(primary = tidy(m, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE),
          observed = tidy(m_observed, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE),
          within_dataset = tidy(m_within, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE),
          .id = "model") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "teaching|^log_age$")) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)
```

## Timing controls

Teaching is entangled with when a test happens. Tests after one exposure come right after it and
early in the session; tests after several exposures come later, after more tests. A flat or
negative teaching slope could reflect fatigue or forgetting rather than a lack of learning.
Three timing variables, from @sec-exposure:

* **position**: `trial_order / session_trials`, 0–1 through the session (centered at .5)
* **test number**: earlier tests of the same word in this session, as log(n + 1)
* **trials since teaching**: trials since the word was last taught in this session, on a log
  scale. Defined only where teaching is part of the imported session (`adams_marchman_2018`,
  `fernald_marchman_2012`, `fernald_totlot`), not where it came from learning videos
  (`reflook_*`, `yurovsky_2017`) or an earlier session.

```{r}
#| label: timing-data
nn_model <- nn_model |>
  mutate(position = trial_order / session_trials - .5,
         log_test = log(test_session + 1),
         log_since_teaching = log(trials_since_teaching))
```

Position and test number are nearly collinear within datasets, so they enter separate models.
In `reflook_socword`, teaching is nearly collinear with both: learning trials and tests are
interleaved in one fixed order.

```{r}
#| label: timing-cor
cor_or_na <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y)
  if (sum(ok) < 3 || sd(x[ok]) == 0 || sd(y[ok]) == 0) NA_real_ else cor(x[ok], y[ok])
}

nn_model |>
  summarise(n_trials = n(),
            prop_since_teaching_defined = mean(!is.na(log_since_teaching)),
            r_teaching_position = cor_or_na(log_teaching, position),
            r_teaching_test = cor_or_na(log_teaching, log_test),
            r_position_test = cor_or_na(position, log_test),
            r_teaching_since = cor_or_na(log_teaching, log_since_teaching),
            .by = dataset_name)
```



### Models

Each model adds one timing control to the primary model. The recency model can only be fit on the
subset where trials-since-teaching is defined, so the primary model is refit on that same subset
for comparison.

```{r}
#| label: timing-models
f_primary <- long_window_accuracy ~ log_teaching * log_age +
  (1 | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id) + (1 | target_label)

nn_since <- nn_model |> filter(!is.na(log_since_teaching))

timing_models <- list(
  "primary" = m,
  "+ position" = lmer(update(f_primary, . ~ . + position), data = nn_model),
  "+ test number" = lmer(update(f_primary, . ~ . + log_test), data = nn_model),
  "primary (recency subset)" = lmer(f_primary, data = nn_since),
  "+ trials since teaching (recency subset)" =
    lmer(update(f_primary, . ~ . + log_since_teaching), data = nn_since)
)

timing_coefs <- timing_models |>
  map(\(x) tidy(x, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "model") |>
  mutate(model = fct_inorder(model),
         n_trials = map_int(timing_models, nobs)[as.character(model)])

timing_coefs |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  select(model, n_trials, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-timing-coefs
#| fig-cap: "Teaching coefficients (±95% CI) with and without timing controls. The teaching slope is for a 24-month-old; the interaction is the change in that slope per unit of log age."
#| fig-height: 3.5
timing_coefs |>
  filter(term %in% c("log_teaching", "log_teaching:log_age")) |>
  mutate(term = recode(term, log_teaching = "log(teaching + 1)",
                       `log_teaching:log_age` = "log(teaching + 1) × log(age / 24)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = fct_rev(model))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high)) +
  facet_wrap(~term, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Estimate", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-timing-pred
#| fig-cap: "Model predictions for accuracy by teaching exposures at representative ages: primary model (dashed) and with position held at mid-session (solid), each over the range of exposures observed within 3 months of that age."
pred_grid_timing <- pred_grid |> mutate(position = 0)

bind_rows(
  primary = pred_grid_timing |> mutate(pred = predict(m, newdata = pred_grid_timing, re.form = NA)),
  `+ position` = pred_grid_timing |>
    mutate(pred = predict(timing_models[["+ position"]], newdata = pred_grid_timing, re.form = NA)),
  .id = "model") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = teaching + 1, y = pred, colour = factor(age), linetype = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(linewidth = .9) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, 33), labels = \(x) x - 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = .9) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(primary = "dashed", `+ position` = "solid")) +
  labs(x = "Teaching exposures (log scale)", y = "Predicted proportion target looking",
       colour = "Age (months)", linetype = "Model")
```
